description:
Problem: NASA's microgravity combustion data is massive and fragmented, complicating fire safety planning for deep space missions.
Idea: IgnisNode is a Super Intelligence (SI) dashboard that instantly retrieves, summarizes, and ranks these findings to deliver actionable fire-safety insights.
Build Plan: I will build a Serverless RAG architecture using a Python/FastAPI backend and an LLM API for context retrieval. The frontend will be a zero-dependency Vanilla JS application featuring.
summary:
IgnisNode is an AI-powered scientific research and decision-support platform that makes NASA microgravity combustion research easier to explore, search, and understand.

The project addresses the challenges of fire safety in space, where microgravity can significantly change flame behavior and make conventional Earth-based assumptions insufficient. Using research material from 10 NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) investigations, IgnisNode combines semantic search, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), and evidence-grounded AI responses to help users investigate scientific findings.

Users can search research documents by meaning, ask scientific questions and receive answers with source citations, explore investigation cards, compare studies, and rank investigations against selected atmospheric reference profiles.

By connecting NASA research with accessible AI-powered tools, IgnisNode helps students and researchers discover relevant evidence and explore its implications for future space habitats.
details:
IgnisNode is a web-based scientific research platform designed to improve access to microgravity combustion research and support evidence-based exploration of fire-safety challenges in space.

How It Works

The platform processes scientific research material from 10 NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) investigations and organizes it into searchable document chunks while preserving relevant investigation identifiers, document references, and metadata.

A vector-based semantic search system allows users to retrieve relevant scientific evidence using natural-language queries. The platform also integrates a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline powered by the Google Gemini API. When users ask a question, IgnisNode retrieves relevant research evidence and uses it to generate an answer with references to supporting source material.

The platform provides several features:

  • Scientific Semantic Search: Find relevant research by meaning rather than exact keyword matching.
  • AI Research Assistant: Ask scientific questions and receive evidence-grounded answers with citations.
  • Investigation Explorer: Browse structured cards representing the supported NASA PSI investigations.
  • Investigation Comparison: Explore similarities and differences between selected investigations.
  • Environmental Reference Profiles: Explore ISS, lunar habitat, spacesuit, and custom atmospheric target profiles.
  • Research-Based Ranking: Rank investigations according to their relevance to selected target conditions.
  • Evidence and Export: Inspect supporting references and export research results.

Benefits and Intended Impact

IgnisNode reduces the effort required to discover and navigate scientific research related to combustion in microgravity. It makes technical research more accessible, supports evidence-based investigation, and helps users explore the relevance of experimental findings to future space-habitat fire-safety challenges.

An important scientific consideration is that the environmental profiles are reference target conditions, not measurements from the original experiments. The platform does not claim that its NASA PSI source investigations provide direct experimental measurements under lunar or Martian partial-gravity conditions. Its outputs are intended for research exploration and decision support, not as certified fire-safety assessments.

Technology and Tools

  • Python 3.12
  • FastAPI
  • Google Gemini API
  • Vector embeddings and semantic retrieval
  • Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
  • HTML, CSS, and JavaScript
  • Chart.js for data visualization
  • Marked for Markdown rendering
  • DOMPurify for HTML sanitization
  • Git and GitHub
  • Ubuntu Linux cloud deployment

Creativity and Original Contribution

The project's original contribution is the integration of NASA PSI research material, semantic retrieval, AI-powered evidence synthesis, citation validation, investigation exploration, and environmental comparison workflows into one accessible scientific platform. Instead of presenting AI-generated answers without context, IgnisNode is designed to connect answers to retrieved research evidence and preserve traceability to the underlying investigations.
